description: Boxarr is an automated box office tracking application that integrates with Radarr to monitor, add, and manage the latest theatrical releases. It provides a beautiful dashboard showing the current box office top 10, their status in your Radarr library, and allows quality profile management.

latest_release.name: Release 2.4.0
latest_release.body:
### Added
- **Optional sign-in**: Boxarr can now ask for a login. Choose it in the new **Settings → Security** section, or by environment variable. The [Authentication](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Authentication) wiki page has the details (#151, #177, #178, #179).
  - **Off** keeps Boxarr as it was: anyone who can reach it can use it.
  - **Forms** is Boxarr's own login page, with a username and password. The password is stored as a scrypt hash in `auth.json`. A session lasts 24 hours, or 90 days with "Keep me signed in"; both lengths can be changed. **Sign out everywhere** ends every other session.
  - **External** lets a reverse proxy that signs people in (Authelia, Authentik and the like) decide. Boxarr passes only requests whose connection comes from an address listed in **Trusted proxies** (`BOXARR_AUTH_TRUSTED_PROXIES`). `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` does not count, and networks broader than /8 (IPv4) or /16 (IPv6) are refused, as are IPv6 zones (`%`). Boxarr can't tell a request the proxy let through without its sign-in from one it signed in, so a path the proxy leaves open is open in Boxarr too.
  - Boxarr has no option to skip sign-in for local addresses. Behind Docker every client can look local, and a website you visit could reach Boxarr through DNS rebinding.
  - Pages without a session go to `/login`. The API answers 401, and a page left open shows a "session expired" banner rather than navigating away, so unsaved input survives.
  - Every setting can come from a `BOXARR_AUTH_*` variable instead, and a variable always wins over Settings: `METHOD`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD_FILE` / `PASSWORD` / `PASSWORD_HASH`, `API_KEY_FILE` / `API_KEY`, `WIDGETS`, `WIDGET_TOKEN`, `TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `COOKIE_SECURE`, `SESSION_HOURS` and `REMEMBER_DAYS`. Settings then shows that field read-only and names the variable. `python -m src.main --hash-password` prints a hash for `BOXARR_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH`.
- **API key for scripts and apps**: with sign-in on, the API takes a `bxk_…` key in the `X-Api-Key` header, or in `Authorization: Bearer`. Create the key in Settings → Security, where it is shown once (Boxarr keeps only its SHA-256), or set it with `BOXARR_AUTH_API_KEY` or `BOXARR_AUTH_API_KEY_FILE`. A key in the URL (`?apikey=`) is refused with a message saying to use the header. A key never opens the Security settings.
- **Widget token**: `/api/widget` and `/api/widget/json` stay public by default, so dashboards keep working. Set **Widgets** to **Token** to require a `bxw_…` token in `?token=`, or `BOXARR_AUTH_WIDGET_TOKEN`. The token opens only the widgets, and Settings shows the embed URLs with it.
- **`--auth-reset`**: `python -m src.main --auth-reset` turns sign-in off, clears the username, password, API key, widget token and settings, and signs everyone out. In Docker the command is `docker exec boxarr python -m src.main --auth-reset`. Use it for a forgotten password, or if someone else turned sign-in on.

### Changed
- **After upgrading, sign-in is off, as before.** Every page shows a banner until you choose: **Set up login** opens Settings → Security, and **Keep it open** hides the banner for good. While sign-in is off, every page and API answer is the same as in 2.3.0, apart from the banner, the Security section and the new `/login` and `/api/auth/*` routes.
- **Until you choose, anyone who can reach Boxarr can turn sign-in on with their own password.** Boxarr makes sure the owner can take it back without the other person keeping access:
  - Turning sign-in off clears the username, the password, the API key, the widget token and the settings.
  - Turning sign-in on always issues a new API key.
  - A save under `BOXARR_AUTH_METHOD=none` (recovery) starts `auth.json` over.
  - A password from the environment that replaces one set in Settings starts `auth.json` over: the API key, the widget token, the trusted proxies and the other saved settings are cleared, and a warning says so. Moving the same password into the environment keep

detail.readme:
# Boxarr - Box Office Tracking for Radarr
**Automatically track and add trending box office movies to your Radarr library** [![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0) [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/docker-ready-brightgreen.svg)](https://www.docker.com/) [![Wiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/wiki-documentation-blue)](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki)
--- Boxarr monitors weekly box office charts and seamlessly integrates with Radarr to ensure your media library always has what people want to watch. No more manual searching for popular movies - Boxarr handles it automatically. ## 🎯 Why Boxarr? - **Stay Current** - Never miss trending movies that everyone's talking about - **Save Time** - No more manually searching for and adding popular films - **Smart Automation** - Automatically add movies based on your preferences - **Family Friendly** - Keep your media server stocked with what people actually want to watch ## 🤔 Why Not Seerr? Seerr is excellent for request-based libraries where users actively request content. Boxarr serves a different purpose: - **Automatic vs Request-Based**: Boxarr automatically adds mainstream hits without anyone having to request them - **Box Office Focus**: Tracks actual commercial success, not just user requests - **Zero User Interaction**: Works silently in the background, no user accounts or requests needed - **Complementary Tool**: Use both! Seerr for specific requests, Boxarr for mainstream coverage ## 📋 Why Not Radarr Lists? While Radarr lists are useful, Boxarr offers unique advantages: - **Box Office = Mainstream Appeal**: Tracks movies with proven commercial success, ensuring broad appeal - **Unbiased Selection**: Based on actual revenue data, not curator preferences or ratings - **Weekly Updates**: Fresh data every week, not dependent on list maintainer updates - **Duplicate Prevention**: Uses Radarr API to check existing movies before adding - **Historical Tracking**: Build a library of movies that were culturally significant at release Boxarr ensures your library includes the mainstream movies that dominated theaters - the films people are most likely to want to watch. ## 📚 Documentation **[View the full documentation in our Wiki](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki)** for detailed guides, configuration options, and troubleshooting. ## ✨ Key Features - **📊 [Weekly Box Office Tracking](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Box-Office-Tracking)** - Automatically fetches the weekend's top movies from Box Office Mojo, for up to 5 regions at once - **🔄 [Radarr Integration](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide#radarr-connection)** - Seamlessly checks and adds movies to your library - **🗂️ [Genre‑Based Root Folders](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Genre-Based-Root-Folders)** - Organize movies into folders by genre - **⚡ [Auto-Add Movies](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide#automation-settings)** - Automatically add trending movies with smart filters - **🔍 [Advanced Custom Filtering](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide#filter-settings)** - Fine-tune selections with genre, rating, and release year filters - **📅 [Scheduled Updates](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide#automation-settings)** - Runs weekly on your preferred schedule - **🎨 [Beautiful Web UI](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Home#-visual-tour)** - Clean, responsive interface for all devices - **🚀 [Easy Setup](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Initial-Setup)** - Simple web-based configuration wizard ## 📋 Requirements - **Radarr** v3.0+ (required) - **Docker** (recommended) or Python 3.10+ - Network access to Box Office Mojo ## 🚀 Quick Start ### Docker (Recommended) ```bash docker run -d \ --name boxarr \ -p 8888:8888 \ -v /path/to/config:/config \ ghcr.io/iongpt/boxarr:latest ``` Visit `http://localhost:8888` and follow the setup wizard. ### Docker Compose ```yaml version: '3.8' services: boxarr: image: ghcr.io/iongpt/boxarr:latest container_name: boxarr ports: - 8888:8888 volumes: - ./config:/config restart: unless-stopped environment: - TZ=America/New_York # Optional: Set your timezone ``` **[View full installation guide →](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Installation-Guide)** ## ⚙️ Initial Setup 1. Open your browser to `http://localhost:8888` 2. Enter your Radarr URL and API key 3. Configure quality profiles and preferences 4. Save and start tracking! **[View detailed setup guide →](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Initial-Setup)** ## 📖 Configuration & Features - **[Box Office Tracking](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Box-Office-Tracking)** - How weekly tracking works - **[Configuration Guide](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide)** - All settings explained - **[Auto-Add Movies](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide#auto-add-movies)** - Automatic movie additions with filters - **[Genre-Based Root Folders](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Genre-Based-Root-Folders)** - Smart content organization - **[API Reference](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/API-Reference)** - REST API documentation ## 🔧 Advanced Configuration ### Reverse Proxy Support Boxarr can run behind reverse proxies (nginx, Traefik, Caddy) with custom URL base support. ```yaml environment: - BOXARR_URL_BASE=boxarr # Access at /boxarr/ ``` **[View reverse proxy setup guide →](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/Configuration-Guide#reverse-proxy-configuration)** ### Box Office Regions & Timeout By default Boxarr tracks the US & Canada domestic chart. Set a Box Office Mojo `area` code to follow a different region, or list up to 5 regions to track several at once, and tune the scraper timeout for slow connections. The setup page offers the same choice as a checkbox list. ```yaml environment: - BOXARR_FEATURES_BOX_OFFICE_REGION=NL # BOM area code (e.g. NL, DE, GB); empty = US & Canada domestic - BOXOFFICE_TIMEOUT=120 # Box Office Mojo request timeout in seconds (default 120, range 5-600) ``` The region setting takes any of these forms; `domestic` stands for the US & Canada chart: | Form | Example | Tracks | |------|---------|--------| | One code | `NL` | the Netherlands | | Comma-separated | `domestic,DE` | US & Canada, then Germany | | JSON list | `["NL","DE"]` | the Netherlands, then Germany | In `local.yaml` the same setting is `boxarr.features.box_office_region`, as a single code or a YAML list (an unquoted `NO`, which YAML reads as `false`, is still taken as Norway). With several regions: - **At most 5 regions** are used; a longer list is cut off with a warning, and the setup page will not save more. - **`box_office_limit` applies per region**: with a limit of 10 and 3 regions, up to 30 chart rows are read each week. - Each week is **one combined list without duplicates**: a film that charted in several regions appears once. The weekly page also shows each region's own chart on its own tab. - **`auto_add_limit` is one cap for the whole run**: at most X movies are added per run, across all your regions, in chart order. Films a filter or the ignore list skips, and films already in Radarr, do not count. - **The minimum-gross filter** compares a film's best weekend gross across its regions. - If a region cannot be fetched, the other regions are still saved: the failed region keeps the chart from the week's previous update when there is one, and the weekly page shows a notice for it. A week saved before multi-region support is left unchanged instead. While `BOXARR_FEATURES_BOX_OFFICE_REGION` is set, it overrides `local.yaml` and the setup page shows the region picker locked. ### API Access Boxarr provides a REST API for integration and automation. - **[Full API Reference →](https://github.com/iongpt/boxarr/wiki/API-Reference)** ## 📸 Screenshots
